item.title: Ford Plants Giant Lake Ontario Sign
item.description:
Ford Plants Giant Lake Ontario Sign

Ontario Premier Doug Ford answered President Trump’s executive order renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America” by unveiling a huge bilingual blue billboard at Fifty Point Conservation Area near Hamilton. The object is not a press release and not a matching decree. It is a physical sign on Canadian ground, large enough to read from the water, planted where a shoreline crowd and a camera phone can both see it. The English face reads “Lake Ontario Now and Always.” The French face reads “Lac Ontario - Aujourd’hui et pour toujours.” Together they are one claim in Canada’s two official languages: the lake already has a name, and that name is not up for a presidential rewrite.

item.title: Ford Unveils Two-Story Name Rebuke
item.description:
Ford Unveils Two-Story Name Rebuke

Ontario Premier Doug Ford answered President Donald Trump’s Thursday order renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America” by unveiling a shoreline billboard Saturday: “Lake Ontario. Now and Always.” The reply was not a diplomatic note and not a matching decree. It was a physical object on Canadian ground, large enough to read as architecture, planted where the water and the cameras could not miss it. CBS said the blue display also reads in French “Lac Ontario - Aujourd’hui et pour toujours” at Fifty Point Conservation Area. Wearing a Team Canada soccer jersey, Ford posed near Grimsby.
